mainTopic: Why only the ראש חודש goat was burned, when פינחס became a כהן, and רב's claim that משה was a כהן גדול
overview: This amud finishes the story of the חטאת that was burned at the inauguration of the משכן. משה admits he heard the law and forgot it. The גמרא then checks the words "היום" and "הן היום" against both רבנן and רבי נחמיה. Next it explains the ברייתא's challenges to רבי נחמיה. Three goats were offered that day, but only the ראש חודש goat was burned, because אנינות does not disqualify one-time offerings. אנינות at night is also Torah law. And פינחס could not eat the offering because he was not yet a כהן, though רבי אלעזר and רב אשי disagree about when he became one. Finally, רב teaches that משה was a כהן גדול who shared in the offerings. The גמרא brings challenges against him, and the last one, about who quarantined מרים, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Moses admits he heard and forgot
steps.stepSummary: From the words "and it was good in his eyes," the גמרא learns that משה was not embarrassed to admit he had forgotten the law.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And it was good in his eyes": משה was not embarrassed and did not say "I never heard this." Instead he said, "I heard it, and I forgot it."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining the end of the story. After אהרן explained himself, משה agreed. The גמרא reads that agreement as an honest admission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה could have covered himself by claiming he had never been taught this law. The פסוק saying he was pleased shows that he admitted the truth: he had been taught it and forgot it. This closes the story before the גמרא asks questions about it.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was good in his eyes (he agreed)
I heard it and I forgot it

steps.whyThisMatters: It is a well-known lesson in honesty. Even משה admitted a mistake openly rather than inventing an excuse.

phrases.english: "And it was good in his eyes":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:20

phrases.english: Moses was not embarrassed to say
"I did not hear,"
rather: "I heard, and I forgot."

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיִּיטַב בְּעֵינָיו לֹא בּוֹשׁ מֹשֶׁה לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story of משה and אהרן from the previous part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה admitted he had heard the law and forgotten it, and he did not claim he had never heard it.

steps.title: Why not wait and eat it at night?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the only problem was eating while in mourning during the day, the כהנים should have waited and eaten the offering that night.
steps.simpleTranslation: They should have held it over and eaten it at night!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story. If eating was only forbidden during the day of mourning, why did they burn the offering instead of waiting until night?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on an אונן eating קדשים applies during the day. At night the problem goes away, and the offering could still be eaten then. So burning it looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: To delay it, to hold it over

phrases.english: They should have delayed it,
and eaten it at night!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the story is finished, the גמרא questions its logic.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Mourning blocks eating only by day, so they could have waited for night instead of burning the offering.

steps.title: It became impure by accident
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the offering became טמא through circumstances no one could control, so it had to be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Impurity came upon it unavoidably.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Waiting was not possible, because the offering became impure, and nobody was at fault for that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impure קדשים cannot be eaten at any time, day or night, so it had to be burned. The word באונס stresses that the כהנים did nothing wrong in letting it become impure.

phrases.english: Impurity came about unavoidably.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about waiting until night.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a fact about what happened
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the offering could have been eaten at night.
steps.terutzMaskana: It became impure unavoidably, so eating it at night was not an option and it had to be burned.

steps.title: What does "today" mean for רבי נחמיה?
steps.stepSummary: The word "היום" fits רבנן well, but what does it mean according to רבי נחמיה?
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבנן, this explains why the פסוק says "today." But for רבי נחמיה, what does "today" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests both opinions against the words of the פסוק. It starts with the word "היום" in אהרן's question, "If I had eaten the חטאת today..."
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבנן, "today" is easy to explain: it is the daytime of mourning, and at night eating would have been allowed. רבי נחמיה, however, explains אהרן's reasoning as a difference between one-time offerings and offerings for all generations, which has nothing to do with day or night. So why would אהרן say "today"?

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (for one side, but...)
The Sages (here רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון)

phrases.english: It works well according to the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: Here רבנן means רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: that is why it is written: "today";
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:19

phrases.english: but according to Rabbi Nechemya,
what is "today"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the logic of the story to checking the wording of the פסוק against each opinion.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word "today" suggests a daytime limit, which seems to fit only רבנן.

steps.title: "Today" means today's obligation
steps.stepSummary: For רבי נחמיה, "today" refers to the offering that was owed that day, the שעיר of ראש חודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means the obligation of the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי נחמיה. "היום" does not mean daytime. It describes which offering was involved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אהרן was saying: "If I had eaten the offering that is today's fixed obligation..." That offering is a קרבן for all generations (ראש חודש), unlike the one-time offerings of the מילואים. So the word fits רבי נחמיה's distinction.

keyTerms.meaning: The offering that is the obligation of the day

phrases.english: The obligation of the day.
phrases.notes: He means the חטאת of ראש חודש, which was owed that day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question on רבי נחמיה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought "today" pointed to a daytime-only ban.
steps.terutzMaskana: "Today" names the offering owed that day, which fits רבי נחמיה.

steps.title: What does "behold, today" mean for the Rabbis?
steps.stepSummary: Now the opposite check: "הן היום" fits רבי נחמיה, but what does it mean according to רבנן?
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי נחמיה, this explains why the פסוק says "behold, today." But for רבנן, what does "behold, today" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the test around and checks another phrase: "Behold, today they offered their חטאת..." This time the question is on רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי נחמיה, "today they offered" again points to the day's obligation, so it fits easily. For רבנן, who read "today" as plain daytime, the phrase "הן היום" seems to have no clear purpose in אהרן's argument.

phrases.english: It works well according to Rabbi Nechemya,
that is why it is written "behold, today";
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:19

phrases.english: but according to the Rabbis,
what is "behold, today"?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב הֵן הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors the previous question, now aimed at רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase "behold, today they offered" fits the idea of the day's obligation, so it seems to have no purpose for רבנן.

steps.title: "Did they offer? I offered!"
steps.stepSummary: For רבנן, אהרן reads "הן" as "they" and says: my sons did not offer it, I did, as כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: Did they offer it? I offered it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבנן by reading "הן" as the word "they" and making it a question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אהרן was telling משה: my sons, who may not serve while mourning, did not bring this offering. I brought it, and a כהן גדול may serve even while an אונן. So the service was valid. The only problem was eating, and that is why the offering was not eaten that day.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he is saying
High Priest, who may serve even while mourning

steps.whatToRemember: Each side explains one phrase easily and reinterprets the other. For רבי נחמיה, "היום" means the day's obligation. For רבנן, "הן" means "they": "Did they offer? I offered!"
steps.confusionAlert: Here "הן" is not read as "behold." רבנן read it as the word "they" (הן), and the line becomes a question.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
Did they offer it?!
phrases.notes: "They" means אהרן's sons. A regular כהן may not serve while mourning.

phrases.english: I offered it!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר הֵן הִקְרִיבוּ אֲנִי הִקְרַבְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question on רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the word as a question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought "הן היום" means "behold, today" and only fits רבי נחמיה.
steps.terutzMaskana: "הן" means "they": my sons did not offer it, I did, as כהן גדול, which is allowed while mourning.

steps.title: Which three offerings should have been burned?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line that 'all three should have been burned' and asks which three offerings are meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: all three of them should have been burned. What does 'all three of them' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the ברייתא: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון told רבי נחמיה that if אנינות were the reason, all three offerings should have been burned. It asks which three offerings this means, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument against רבי נחמיה only works if we know which offerings were brought that day. So before judging the argument, the גמרא first needs to know what 'three' refers to.

phrases.english: The Master said:
All three of them should have been burned.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: What does "all three of them" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from discussing the word 'היום' to another line in the same ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which three offerings the ברייתא means when it says all three should have been burned.

steps.title: The three goats hinted at in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads three offerings into the פסוק: נחשון's goat, the eighth-day חטאת, and the ראש חודש goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'And the goat of the sin offering משה diligently inquired.' 'Goat' is נחשון's goat. 'Sin offering' is the חטאת of the eighth day. 'Inquired' is the goat of ראש חודש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that finds three different goats in three words of one פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word points to a different goat that was offered on that same day. That gives us the 'three' in the ברייתא: one from the נשיא נחשון, one for the eighth day of the inauguration, and one for ראש חודש.

keyTerms.meaning: נחשון, the נשיא of שבט יהודה, who brought the first נשיא's offering
the sin offering of the eighth day of the inauguration

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:
"And Moshe diligently inquired for the goat of the sin offering";
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:16

phrases.english: "Goat": this is the goat of נחשון,
phrases.notes: This is the goat in the נשיא's offering on the first day of the inauguration (במדבר 7:12-16).

phrases.english: "Sin offering": this is the sin offering of the eighth day,
"Inquired": this is the goat of ראש חודש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The three are נחשון's goat, the eighth-day חטאת, and the ראש חודש goat.

steps.title: Only one was burned, and משה asked twice
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: 'it was burned' shows only one goat was burned, and the doubled word 'inquired' shows משה asked two questions.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think all three were burned. So the פסוק says 'and behold, it was burned': one was burned, not all three. Why does it say 'inquired, inquired', two inquiries? משה asked them: why was this sin offering burned, and why were these others left?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and shows from the פסוק that only one of the three goats was burned. It also reads the doubled word as two questions from משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'שרף' is singular, so only one goat was burned. משה's two questions were: why was this one burned, and why were the other two not burned? That is exactly the difference רבי נחמיה will need to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: "inquire, he inquired": a doubled word, read here as two inquiries

phrases.english: One might think all three of them were burned?
The verse teaches: "and behold, it was burned"
phrases.notes: The word is singular, "it", so it points to only one goat.

phrases.english: one was burned
and not all three of them were burned.
"Diligently inquired": why two inquiries?
He said to them:
Why was this sin offering burned,
and these are left alone?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only one of the three goats was burned, and משה asked why that one was burned while the others were not.

steps.title: The burned one was the ראש חודש goat
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא identifies the burned goat as the ראש חודש goat, because it 'bears the sin of the congregation'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I still don't know which one was burned. When the פסוק says 'And He gave it to you to bear the sin of the congregation', you must say this is the ראש חודש goat.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by showing which of the three goats was burned: the ראש חודש goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes the burned goat as one that atones for the whole community. That fits the ראש חודש goat, so that is the one that was burned. The other two were left.

keyTerms.meaning: but I do not know which one it is

steps.whatToRemember: Three goats were offered that day: נחשון's, the eighth-day חטאת, and the ראש חודש goat. Only the ראש חודש goat was burned.

phrases.english: But I do not know which one it is;
when it says:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְאֹתָהּ נָתַן לָכֶם לָשֵׂאת אֶת עֲוֹן הָעֵדָה״,
phrases.english: "And He gave it to you to bear the sin of the congregation",
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:17

phrases.aramaic: הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר זֶה שָׂעִיר שֶׁל רֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: you must say this is the goat of ראש חודש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the ברייתא by naming which goat was burned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The burned goat was the ראש חודש goat.

steps.title: The question against רבי נחמיה is a strong one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון made a good point: if mourning were the reason, all three goats should have been burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are saying it well to him!
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know the three goats, the גמרא agrees that רבי נחמיה's opponents have a strong argument. This sets up the answer for רבי נחמיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אנינות affected אהרן and his sons equally for all three offerings. So if אנינות made the ראש חודש goat unfit, it should have made the other two unfit too. Yet only one was burned.

keyTerms.meaning: they are saying it well to him: their argument is a strong one
the state of a mourner on the day a close relative dies

phrases.english: They are saying it well to him!
phrases.notes: "They" are רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, and "him" is רבי נחמיה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the facts from the ברייתא to show the argument against רבי נחמיה is strong.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי נחמיה's view that the goat was burned because of אנינות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אנינות applied the same way to all three goats, so all three should have been burned. But only one was.

steps.title: Mourning does not disqualify one-time offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה holds that אנינות does not disqualify קדשי שעה, so only the permanent ראש חודש offering was disqualified and burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה follows his own reasoning, for he said: mourning does not disqualify one-time offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי נחמיה by pointing to another view he holds: אנינות only disqualifies offerings that apply for all generations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נחשון's goat and the eighth-day חטאת were one-time offerings for the inauguration (קדשי שעה), so אנינות did not make them unfit. The ראש חודש goat is brought for all generations (קדשי דורות), so it was made unfit and had to be burned. That explains why only one goat was burned.

keyTerms.meaning: following his own reasoning (a view he holds elsewhere)
offerings for a one-time occasion only

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי נחמיה, אנינות disqualified only the ראש חודש goat, which is brought for all generations. The two one-time goats were not affected.

phrases.english: רבי נחמיה follows his own reasoning,
for he said:
offerings for a one-time occasion
mourning does not disqualify them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to another view the same תנא holds (לטעמיה), which divides the offerings into two types.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אנינות should disqualify all three goats equally.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי נחמיה, אנינות disqualifies only קדשי דורות, so only the ראש חודש goat was burned.

steps.title: Why not eat it at night?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's challenge that the כהנים could have eaten the offering in the evening, and admits this is a strong question.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: He should have eaten it in the evening. They are making a good point to him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא and quotes another challenge רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון raised against רבי נחמיה. It agrees the question is a good one, which sets up an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה said the goat was burned because the כהנים were mourners (אוננים). The challenge is that mourning only blocks eating during the day. So the כהנים could have waited until night and eaten it then, instead of burning it.

keyTerms.meaning: They are making a good point to him

phrases.english: The Master said:
He should have eaten it in the evening.
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון's challenge in the ברייתא, aimed at רבי נחמיה.

phrases.english: They are making a good point to him!
phrases.notes: In other words: this is a strong question, so how would רבי נחמיה answer it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: הָיָה לוֹ לְאׇכְלָהּ לָעֶרֶב. שַׁפִּיר קָאָמְרִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבי נחמיה on why only one goat was burned, the גמרא turns to another challenge in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי נחמיה's claim that the goat was burned because of אנינות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Mourning blocks eating only during the day. So the offering could have been eaten at night and did not need to be burned.

steps.title: Mourning at night is Torah law
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה holds that אנינות at night is also Torah law, so the כהנים could not eat the offering at night either.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that mourning at night is from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי נחמיה: in his view, the night after the death still counts as Torah-level mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that night would be permitted. רבי נחמיה holds that אנינות at night is a Torah law too. So waiting until evening would not help, and the offering had to be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: The mourner's status during the night after the death

phrases.english: He holds: mourning at night is from the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The answer shows a different underlying view: רבי נחמיה holds that night mourning is Torah law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The challenge assumed night was free of אנינות, so the offering could have been eaten then.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי נחמיה, אנינות continues at night by Torah law, so the offering could not be eaten at all.

steps.title: Wasn't פינחס there to eat it?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון challenge: פינחס was not a mourner, so he could have eaten the offering. The גמרא again admits it is a good question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another point: wasn't פינחס with them? They are making a good point to him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a second challenge from the ברייתא. It again agrees the question is strong, which sets up an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if אהרן and his sons were mourners, פינחס (אלעזר's son) was not a mourner. Then a כהן was available who could eat it, so why burn it? This attacks the idea that mourning was the reason.

phrases.english: Another point:
But wasn't פינחס with them?
phrases.notes: He means: פינחס wasn't a mourner, so he could have eaten it.

phrases.english: They are making a good point to him!

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: וַהֲלֹא פִּינְחָס הָיָה עִמָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate challenge from the same ברייתא against רבי נחמיה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי נחמיה's claim that the goat was burned because of אנינות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A non-mourning כהן (פינחס) was present and could have eaten it. So mourning cannot explain why it was burned.

steps.title: פינחס was not yet a כהן
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה agrees with רבי אלעזר, who says that פינחס only became a כהן after he killed זמרי. That happened later than the משכן's inauguration.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי אלעזר, for רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי חנינא: פינחס did not become a כהן until he killed זמרי, as it is written: 'And it shall be for him and his descendants after him a covenant of eternal priesthood.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that פינחס could not eat the offering, because at that time he was not yet a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only כהנים may eat this offering. According to רבי אלעזר, פינחס received כהונה only as a reward for killing זמרי, which happened years later. So at the inauguration only the mourning כהנים were around, and nobody could eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like (agrees with) a certain opinion
The man פינחס killed for sinning with a Midianite woman

phrases.english: He holds like רבי אלעזר,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: for רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי חנינא:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִתְכַּהֵן פִּינְחָס עַד שֶׁהֲרָגוֹ לְזִמְרִי,
phrases.english: פינחס did not become a כהן until he killed זמרי,
phrases.notes: See במדבר 25:6–8.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'And it shall be for him and his descendants after him
a covenant of eternal priesthood.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 25:13

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual answer: פינחס did not yet have כהונה at that time, which is learned from a פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פינחס was a כהן who was not a mourner, so he could have eaten it.
steps.terutzMaskana: פינחס became a כהן only after killing זמרי, so at the inauguration he could not eat קדשים.
steps.confusionAlert: פינחס was the grandson of אהרן, but he was born before his family was made כהנים. So he was not automatically a כהן. That is why he needed to become one later.

steps.title: רב אשי: Even later, after making peace
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says פינחס became a כהן only when he made peace between the tribes, in the days of יהושע. The proof is that he is first called 'the כהן' there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: until he made peace between the tribes, as it says: 'And פינחס the כהן, and the leaders of the congregation, and the heads of the thousands of Israel heard…'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different view of when פינחס became a כהן. Either way, he was not a כהן at the inauguration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב אשי, the moment פינחס became a כהן was even later, in the time of יהושע. He brings proof from a פסוק that calls him 'פינחס הכהן' in that story. Under both opinions, the answer to the challenge about פינחס still works.

keyTerms.meaning: 'פינחס the כהן' — the title that shows he was a כהן

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
until he made peace between the tribes,
phrases.notes: He means: פינחס did not become a כהן until then.

phrases.english: as it says: 'And פינחס the כהן heard,

phrases.aramaic: וּנְשִׂיאֵי הָעֵדָה וְרָאשֵׁי אַלְפֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: and the leaders of the congregation, and the heads of the thousands of Israel, etc.'
phrases.notes: יהושע 22:30

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: עַד שֶׁשָּׂם שָׁלוֹם בֵּין הַשְּׁבָטִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different view from רבי אלעזר on when פינחס became a כהן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פינחס became a כהן only when he made peace between the tribes in יהושע's time.

steps.title: What about the covenant פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי: the פסוק after the זמרי story already gives פינחס the covenant of priesthood.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for the other one too — isn't it written: 'And it shall be for him and his descendants after him'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רב אשי deals with the פסוק that רבי אלעזר used. That פסוק seems to show that פינחס became a כהן right after killing זמרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah already gives פינחס a covenant of priesthood after the זמרי story, he seems to be a כהן from then on. That is a problem for רב אשי, who says it happened only much later.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other opinion)

phrases.english: And the other one too,
phrases.notes: 'The other one' is רב אשי.

phrases.english: isn't it written: 'And it shall be for him and his descendants after him'?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's view in Step 18 using רבי אלעזר's פסוק from Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's view that פינחס became a כהן only in יהושע's time
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The covenant פסוק comes right after the זמרי story, so it seems to make him a כהן already then.

steps.title: The covenant was a blessing for later
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reads the covenant פסוק as a blessing promising future כהונה, not as making פינחס a כהן right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that פסוק is written, it is written as a blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב אשי: the פסוק was a promise about the future, not the moment פינחס actually became a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'for him and his descendants after him' are a blessing that כהונה would come to him and stay in his family. They do not prove that it took effect right away. So רב אשי can still hold that it began only when he made peace between the tribes.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees פינחס was not a כהן at the inauguration of the משכן, so he could not eat the offering. רבי אלעזר says he became a כהן after killing זמרי. רב אשי says it was only when he made peace between the tribes. For רב אשי, the covenant פסוק was a blessing about the future.

phrases.english: When that is written,
it is written as a blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי כְתִיב הָהוּא, בִּבְרָכָה הוּא דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק: it is a promise about the future, not the moment it happened.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The covenant פסוק made פינחס a כהן right after he killed זמרי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק is a blessing for future כהונה. It actually began later, when he made peace between the tribes.

steps.title: How does the other view explain 'פינחס the כהן' in יהושע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the view of רבי אלעזר, that פינחס became a כהן right after זמרי. It asks how that view explains the פסוק in יהושע, which calls him 'the כהן' only later.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other view too: isn't it written, 'And פינחס the כהן heard'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges the other side, which says פינחס became a כהן right after killing זמרי. It asks how that side deals with רב אשי's proof פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי proved his view from the פסוק in יהושע that calls פינחס 'the כהן' at the peace-making with the tribes. If פינחס was already a כהן since the זמרי story, why does the title seem to show up for the first time only there? Now each side has a פסוק it must explain.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other opinion)
And פינחס the כהן heard (a פסוק in יהושע)

phrases.english: And the other one also,
phrases.notes: He means the view of רבי אלעזר, that פינחס became a כהן right after the זמרי story.

phrases.english: isn't it written:
"And Pinchas the priest heard"!
phrases.notes: יהושע 22:30

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב אשי's reading of the covenant פסוק, the גמרא now puts the opposite view under the same pressure.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רבי אלעזר, that פינחס became a כהן after killing זמרי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק in יהושע calls him 'the כהן' only at the later event, which suggests he became a כהן only then.

steps.title: The title is there to link his descendants to him
steps.stepSummary: Calling פינחס 'the כהן' in יהושע is not when he became a כהן. It is there to give his descendants their lineage through him.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק is to give his descendants after him their family line.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the title 'the כהן' in יהושע has a different job. It is not marking the moment he became a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this view, פינחס was already a כהן from the זמרי story. The title in יהושע serves to set up his family line as כהנים through him. So the פסוק does not prove he only became a כהן at that point.

keyTerms.meaning: To give a family line, to trace lineage

phrases.english: That one is to give lineage to his descendants after him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 21 by giving the title in יהושע a different purpose.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the purpose of a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The title 'the כהן' in יהושע shows when פינחס first became a כהן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The title is there to give his descendants their lineage, not to mark when his כהונה began.
steps.whatToRemember: Both views can explain both פסוקים. רב אשי says he became a כהן in the days of יהושע, and the covenant פסוק is a blessing for the future. The other view says he became a כהן after זמרי, and the title in יהושע sets up his descendants' lineage.

steps.title: רב: מֹשֶׁה was a כהן גדול who got a share of the offerings
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ was a כהן גדול and took a share of קָדָשִׁים. His proof is the פסוק saying part of the inauguration ram was 'a portion for מֹשֶׁה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ was a כהן גדול and took a share of holy offerings, as it says: 'from the inauguration ram, it was a portion for מֹשֶׁה'.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רב says that מֹשֶׁה had the status of a כהן גדול and received a share of the offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is ויקרא 8:29: during the seven days of inauguration, the breast of the ram was 'a portion for מֹשֶׁה'. Since he got a portion like a כהן, רב concludes that he was a כהן with a share in קָדָשִׁים.

keyTerms.meaning: Receives a share of holy offerings
The ram of the inauguration (of the כהנים)

phrases.english: Rav said:
Moses our teacher was a High Priest
and he would take a share in offerings consecrated to Heaven,
as it is stated:
"Of the ram of inauguration, it was Moses' portion."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 8:29

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ – כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching. It connects to the discussion of who in the משכן could eat the offerings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מֹשֶׁה was a כהן גדול and was entitled to a share of קָדָשִׁים, proven from his portion of the inauguration ram.

steps.title: Why didn't the ברייתא say 'מֹשֶׁה was with them'?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asked, 'Wasn't פינחס with them?' If מֹשֶׁה could eat offerings, it should have asked, 'Wasn't מֹשֶׁה with them?'
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: the ברייתא says 'Wasn't פינחס with them?' If רב is right, it should say 'Wasn't מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ with them?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב from the ברייתא we saw earlier. There, רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון said a non-mourner (פינחס) could have eaten the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that ברייתא, the argument was that a non-mourning כהן was available to eat the חטאת. If מֹשֶׁה was a כהן who shared in offerings, he was the most obvious example to name. Since they named פינחס and not מֹשֶׁה, it seems מֹשֶׁה could not eat offerings.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
But wasn't Pinchas with them?
phrases.notes: This is the line from the ברייתא of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון back in Step 16.

phrases.english: And if it is so,
phrases.notes: He means: if רב is right that משה shared in offerings.

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא: וַהֲלֹא מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ הָיָה עִמָּהֶן!
phrases.english: let it say: But wasn't Moses our teacher with them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's teaching from Step 23 using the ברייתא quoted in Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that מֹשֶׁה shared in the offerings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא pointed to פינחס, not מֹשֶׁה, as the available eater. This suggests מֹשֶׁה was not someone who could eat.

steps.title: מֹשֶׁה was busy with the שכינה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא may have skipped מֹשֶׁה because he was always busy with the שכינה. We know this from the teaching that he went up and came down early in the morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps מֹשֶׁה is different, because he was busy with the שכינה. As the Master said: מֹשֶׁה went up early in the morning and came down early in the morning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב. מֹשֶׁה was allowed to eat, but he was not free to do so, because he was always busy with the שכינה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not take away מֹשֶׁה's status as a כהן. It only explains why he was not a practical choice to eat the offering. The proof is that his whole schedule was taken up with speaking to ה׳, from early in the morning.

phrases.english: Perhaps Moses is different,
since he was busy with the Divine Presence;
as the Master said:
Moses went up early in the morning
phrases.notes: This means going up הר סיני.

phrases.english: and came down early in the morning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 24 and keeps רב's teaching standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: He had the right, but was not available
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the ברייתא did not name מֹשֶׁה, he could not eat offerings.
steps.terutzMaskana: מֹשֶׁה could eat, but he was too busy with the שכינה, so the ברייתא named פינחס instead.
steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not say מֹשֶׁה was not a כהן. It only says he was not free in practice to eat that offering.

steps.title: A new ברייתא: why does the פסוק name both kinds of offerings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on the פסוק about a כהן with a מום eating 'the most holy and the holy' offerings. It asks why both kinds need to be stated. The challenge to רב continues afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: 'The bread of his God, from the most holy and from the holy, he may eat.' If the most holy offerings were stated, why state the lesser offerings? And if the lesser offerings were stated, why state the most holy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge to רב from a ברייתא. Here the ברייתא only opens with its question about the פסוק, and how this hurts רב will come out as it continues.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says a כהן with a מום may eat both קָדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים and קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים. The ברייתא asks why both are needed: it seems that stating one should be enough, whichever way you look at it. Its answer, and how it bears on מֹשֶׁה, comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The bread of his God (the offerings)
Offerings of the most holy level

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
"The bread of his God, of the most holy
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:22, about a כהן with a מום.

phrases.english: and of the holy, he may eat" –
if the most holy offerings were stated,
why were offerings of lesser holiness stated?
phrases.notes: Some versions say נאמר, in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, is נֶאֶמְרוּ. Both mean 'stated'.

phrases.english: And if offerings of lesser holiness were stated,
why were the most holy offerings stated?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge to רב was answered, the גמרא opens a second challenge from a different ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that מֹשֶׁה was a כהן גדול who shared in offerings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here the ברייתא only begins, by asking why the פסוק names both kinds of offerings. The point against רב will come as the ברייתא continues.

steps.title: Why the פסוק needs both kinds of offerings
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that each kind of offering had to be stated. From only one, we would have wrongly limited a כהן with a מום to that kind alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the פסוק had not mentioned קדשים קלים, I would have said a כהן with a מום eats only קדשי קדשים, since those were permitted even to a זר as well as to כהנים. But he could not eat קדשים קלים. If it had not mentioned קדשי קדשים, I would have said he eats קדשים קלים because they are lighter, but not קדשי קדשים. That is why both are stated.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question from step 26. It shows that each half of the פסוק teaches something we could not have figured out alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each kind of offering has a reason to think a כהן with a מום could eat only that kind. קדשי קדשים were permitted even to a זר, so they seem less restricted. קדשים קלים are lower in holiness, so they seem easier to allow. Since logic could go either way, the תורה spells out both.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said (a mistaken assumption)
That is why they were stated

steps.confusionAlert: Don't miss the strange phrase 'permitted to a זר'. Normally a non-כהן may never eat קדשי קדשים. The גמרא is about to ask exactly who this זר was.

phrases.english: Had offerings of lesser holiness not been stated,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the round-bracket word; the square-bracket word is the corrected wording. The meaning is the same.

phrases.aramaic: הָיִיתִי אוֹמֵר: קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים הוּא דְּאוֹכֵל,
phrases.english: I would have said: it is the most holy offerings that he eats,
since they were permitted to a non-כהן and to them;
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the כהנים.

phrases.english: but offerings of lesser holiness he may not eat.
And had the most holy offerings not been stated,

phrases.aramaic: הָיִיתִי אוֹמֵר: בְּקָדָשִׁים קַלִּים יְהֵא אוֹכֵל,
phrases.english: I would have said: he may eat offerings of lesser holiness,
since they are lighter;
but the most holy offerings he may not eat.
Therefore the most holy offerings were stated,
and therefore the offerings of lesser holiness were stated.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילּוּ לֹא נֶאֶמְרוּ קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים, הָיִיתִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's own question from step 26 about why both kinds are stated. This is still part of the quoted source, and the point against רב comes in step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each half of the פסוק blocks a different wrong assumption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כהן with a מום eats only one kind: either קדשי קדשים (permitted to a זר) or קדשים קלים (lighter)
steps.terutzMaskana: He eats both kinds, so both must be written

steps.title: Who is the non-כהן allowed to eat the holiest offerings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא picks out the phrase 'permitted to a זר'. It suggests the זר is משה, which would mean משה was not a כהן, against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any event, the ברייתא teaches: 'since they were permitted to a זר and to them.' Isn't that זר משה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to its challenge against רב. It uses one detail from the ברייתא it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only obvious non-כהן who ate קדשי קדשים is משה, who ate from the inauguration offerings. If the ברייתא calls him a זר, then משה was not a כהן גדול. That contradicts רב in step 23.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not…? (opens a pointed suggestion)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is why the גמרא quoted the whole ברייתא. The detail about a זר is the real ammunition against רב.

phrases.english: In any event, it teaches:
'since they were permitted to a non-כהן and to them.'
Is this not referring to משה?
phrases.notes: משה ate from the inauguration offerings, so the ברייתא would be calling him a זר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses a detail from the ברייתא in step 27 to challenge רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement that משה was a כהן גדול (step 23)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls whoever ate קדשי קדשים a זר. That must be משה, so משה was not a כהן.

steps.title: רב ששת: the ברייתא means a non-כהן at a private altar
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the זר is not משה. It is a non-כהן offering on a private altar (במה). This follows the view that a מנחה could be brought on a במה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: No. It refers to a non-כהן on a private altar, following the view that says a מנחה may be offered on a private altar.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת defends רב. He finds a different זר the ברייתא could mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the times when private altars were allowed, even a non-כהן could serve on them. A מנחה is קדשי קדשים. So according to the view that a מנחה could be offered on a במה, a זר would have eaten קדשי קדשים there. The ברייתא no longer has to mean משה, so רב stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Private altar, allowed during certain periods
Meal offering, which is קדשי קדשים

phrases.english: רב ששת said: No;
it refers to a non-כהן on a private altar,
and following the one who says: there is a meal offering on a private altar.
phrases.notes: A מנחה is קדשי קדשים, so this view lets a זר have קדשי קדשים at a במה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28 by changing who the זר is.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets which case the ברייתא means
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The זר who had קדשי קדשים must be משה
steps.terutzMaskana: The זר is someone offering on a במה, under the view that a מנחה was offered there

steps.title: A new challenge: who quarantined מרים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new challenge to רב. It asks who quarantined מרים when she had צרעת, and argues it could not be משה because he was a זר. The challenge continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: Who quarantined מרים? If you say משה quarantined her, but משה was a non-כהן,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge against רב from another ברייתא. The argument is not finished yet; it continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a כהן can look at צרעת and declare a quarantine. This ברייתא calls משה a זר, so he could not have quarantined מרים. That suggests משה was not a כהן, against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: משה's sister, who was struck with צרעת
Quarantined her, a step only a כהן may declare

phrases.english: They raised an objection: Who quarantined מרים?
phrases.notes: במדבר 12:10

phrases.english: If you say משה quarantined her,
but משה was a non-כהן,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב ששת answers the first challenge, the גמרא brings a fresh challenge to רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that משה was a כהן גדול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Quarantining for צרעת needs a כהן. The ברייתא says משה could not do it because he was a זר.
